claims.supported_claim: Each connection starts its own OS thread with bounded command channel. Execute has bounded row channel. Row send failure stops iteration; this does not preempt sqlite3_step already executing.
limitations: A bounded row/item channel does not prove retained bytes bounded; NativeWeave must bound connection threads, accepted work, row bytes, and waiting payloads.

claims.supported_claim: Begin success with lost acknowledgement triggers immediate rollback; rollback failure exits the worker. Successful Commit/Rollback with lost ack sets ignore_next_start_rollback to avoid rolling back a completed transaction when the Transaction later drops.
limitations: Worker acknowledgement is not the C# application result, and lost acknowledgement must not be translated into a false rollback conclusion. Custom BEGIN validation moved into worker in 0.9.

claims.supported_claim: start_rollback and shutdown synchronously send into the bounded command channel. Shutdown handling drops connection references before ack and then exits its loop.
limitations: These send calls can block. They must not run directly in NativeWeave nonblocking request_stop/try_retire/ReleaseHandle/reverse callback. Ack occurs before closure return; it is not an OS JoinHandle proof.

claims.supported_claim: Graceful close may execute PRAGMA optimize, then requests worker shutdown, drops self and awaits confirmation. close_hard drops self and immediately returns; flush is no-op.
limitations: close_hard/Drop/flush are not proof of worker completion or NativeWeave quiescence. Run potentially blocking cleanup from a controlled native blocking lane/supervisor, keep ownership until confirmed.

claims.supported_claim: Progress handler uses owned boxed closure, only one handler per connection; false interrupts, replacement removes/frees old handler. C shim catch_unwind maps ordinary panic to interrupt. ConnectionState clears statements before hook removal and handle drop.
limitations: Handler must not modify the connection; avoid arbitrary managed user callbacks or allocations per VM poll. Its catch/unwrap_or_default does not imply universal panic-payload destructor safety.

claims.supported_claim: Statement reset/clear_bindings precede bind. step yields row/result/error; dropping iterator calls statement.reset().ok().
limitations: Drop swallows reset failure; NativeWeave needs an explicit reuse proof or conservative discard, not 'Drop means clean'. StatementHandle::reset internals not read in this task.

claims.supported_claim: begin/commit/rollback delegate to worker; start_rollback only enqueues and ignores the enqueue error at manager boundary; depth is separately observed.
limitations: No executed transaction/cancellation test in this research.

claims.supported_claim: Tests assert progress-triggered interrupted database error and correct closure-state identity; repeated handler replacement preserves expected Arc strong count and removal frees the captured owner.
limitations: Test source read, not executed; does not cover all cancellation/close/next-operation races.

claims.supported_claim: Executor passes query arguments and SqlStr to worker, exposes result receiver as stream; optional fetch limits rows.
limitations: 0.9 SQL and argument ownership/signatures changed. SqlSafeStr/AssertSqlSafe requirements must be respected; not equivalent to SQL semantic validation or ORM.

suggested_nativeweave_policy: Use SQLx SQLite's existing per-connection worker, bound connections and queue/row bytes; do not add an unbounded second worker layer.

Install the native-only progress handler before query execution while holding LockedSqliteHandle; capture a distinct operation cancellation state. request_cancel merely sets that state's atomic flag without calling lock_handle or waiting for worker capacity.

After statement/receiver completion and reset or discard, remove the operation handler under the same serialized connection discipline before returning the connection. Late managed cancellation must not affect the next operation; operation state/registration must drain first.

Cancellation is cooperative and not a universal hard deadline: SQLite busy/extension/filesystem paths may not poll the progress callback promptly. Keep worker, parent leases, budget and cleanup obligations while work remains.

Drop/reset .ok() or close_hard cannot serve as provider-ready oracle. Use explicit coordinator completion and connection-specific safety checks, otherwise discard; never report successful DisposeAsync before NativeWeave-local drain.

SQLx driver mechanisms do not satisfy the user-required Rust ORM by themselves. ORM version and transitive SQLx feature versions must be selected coherently; this 0.9 source study does not force an incompatible upgrade.
